To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) humans are able to attribute intentionality and autonomy to virtual agents, which (2) in turn can be used to establish cooperative relations with these agents, and (3) these cooperative relations can be used to achieve joint action goals, such as the joint execution of a complex task.

the following factors contribute to successful embodied cooperation: (a) the ability to adopt the perspective of others, (b) the ability to take initiative, (c) the ability to represent the other’s goals and actions, and (d) the ability to act together to achieve shared goals.

(i) humans and virtual agents can interact as if they are embodied in the same space and (ii) the interaction is based on a common representation of the virtual world and a common understanding of the other’s intentions and goals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computational model for embodied cooperative systems that is based on the notion of joint attention and joint intentions.
the development of artificial agents which can interact with humans in cooperative settings.
understanding and modeling the processes involved when two individuals cooperate, and how these can be realized in embodied cooperative systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the embodied cooperative system “Max” is a “partnership”, insofar it is an autonomous system that is able to take initiative, and insofar it can understand the intentions of others and represent them as being able understand intentions.

the interplay of the different processes involved in cooperation is still not well understood and that the modeling of these processes is still at an early stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are currently able to endow Max with the capacity to understand the intentions of a human interlocutor in a cooperative task, to represent the other as being able to do so, and to act in accordance with this representation.
the development of embodied cooperative systems requires a multi-disciplinary approach that integrates research in cognitive science, computer science, and robotics.

we have shown that it is possible to endow artificial agents with the capability of taking initiative in the pursuit of joint goals, and to do this in a way that is grounded in the agent’s perception of the environment and the agent’s own embodiment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a virtual humanoid agent, when interacting with a human partner, may become a partner in its own right, and that it can be endowed with cooperative functionality.
embodied cooperative systems are a useful tool for understanding the processes underlying human social interaction.
the ability to represent others’ goals and intentions is a key factor in cooperative settings.
